topicName: Node Operations: Running Full Nodes, Archive Nodes, and Validator Setup
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Node Operations: Running Full Nodes, Archive Nodes, and Validator Setup in Web3"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Participating in blockchain networks requires understanding the different types of nodes and how to set them up securely. This tutorial covers the operational differences between full nodes, archive nodes, and validators, along with practical configuration steps."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Node Types"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Full Nodes: Store a condensed version of the blockchain state, typically verifying blocks and state transitions without keeping historical states indefinitely."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Archive Nodes: Maintain the complete historical state of the blockchain from genesis. Essential for querying past balances, smart contract states, and debugging historical transactions."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Validator Nodes: Active participants in proof-of-stake or consensus protocols that propose and validate new blocks to secure the network and earn rewards."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Setting Up a Full Node"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To run a production-grade full node, you typically use containerized environments or direct binary execution. Below is an example using Docker for an Ethereum-compatible client like Geth."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"docker run -d --name eth-full-node -v /mnt/nvme/geth:/root/.ethereum -p 8545:8545 -p 30303:30303 ethereum/client-geth:latest --mainnet --http --http.addr '0.0.0.0' --http.api 'eth,net,web3'"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Configuring an Archive Node"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Archive nodes require significant storage capacity (often several terabytes) because they do not prune historical state data. Modify the client flags to disable state pruning."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"docker run -d --name eth-archive-node -v /mnt/nvme/archive:/root/.ethereum -p 8546:8545 ethereum/client-geth:latest --mainnet --gcmode archive --http --http.api 'eth,net,web3,debug'"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Validator Node Setup and Key Generation"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Validators require two components: an execution client and a consensus client. First, generate your validator keys using the official staking deposit CLI."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"./staking-deposit-cli deposit-cli new-mnemonic --num_validators=1 --chain=mainnet"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once keys are generated and imported into your consensus client, start both clients with validator duties enabled. Ensure your fee recipient address is properly configured to collect transaction tips."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"lighthouse validator_client --beacon-node http://localhost:5052 --keystore /path/to/keystores --suggested-fee-recipient 0xYourWalletAddressHere"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Monitoring and Security Best Practices"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Firewall Configuration: Restrict P2P ports to necessary IPs and keep RPC endpoints private or behind a reverse proxy like Nginx."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Metrics & Alerting: Integrate Prometheus and Grafana to track sync status, peer counts, slot participation rates, and disk space usage."}]
